questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I've always wanted to go to Edinburgh to study as it's a really lovely city and campus. I also wanted to go to an English speaking country

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Loved being in Edinburgh - the academics were not as good as I had imagined, but I mostly came for the rest of the experience, so it didn't matter much to me

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I think they were pretty good at keeping us informed, they sent out a lot of e-mails and there was also a couple of online meetings beforehand. They were generally quite fast at responding to e-mails too.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was another online meeting, a brunch event for psychology exchange students and you could come by the exchange office.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was pretty hard to find housing in Edinburgh as they're having a housing crisis. They don't let you know whether you'll get student accommodation until very late. Sign up for the student accommodation as soon as you can, but you should also call them in the last couple of weeks. That's how all of us got accommodation. I hadn't signed up until quite late, but their system doesn't really work, so you probably won't get anything unless you call. If you want to find accommodation on your own it might be easier to be in Edinburgh while looking.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: You can't really live on campus in Edinburgh (just like in Copenhagen), but a lot of student accommodation is pretty close to campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Student accommodation is so expensive, but it was pretty much the only choice we had - it was at least with all bills included. The standard of the housing can be really different from dorm to dorm. Mine was newly built, so it was pretty good, but I shared common room/kitchen with people who didn't know how to clean up after themselves.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You had to choose some courses when you did your application, but these didn't really count as you couldn't choose all of the ones that was actually available. Afterwards you just had to fill out a form to change them.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I think they sent out e-mails that described the process pretty well. You could also send them an e-mail. They even send me a reminder, because I forgot to change one of my classes.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Yes.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Get your forhåndsgodkendelser at UCPH at soon as possible. They won't change your courses unless you have one. If you register for courses on time, I'm pretty sure you will get the ones that you want without problem. Some of the other exchange students struggled a bit, but it all worked out in the end. I took two courses that was not in the psychology department, so remember to look at courses at other departments as you might find the ones you'll need there.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I was a bit surprised that it was a lot easier than at UCPH. I didn't have a lot of lectures or classes and we didn't really do much in the classes, although that may just have been the specific classes that I picked. There were also less readings/more freedom to choose what you wanted to read. But I wasn't really there for the academics, so I thought it was just nice to have more time to have fun.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Easier than at UCPH. You're not expected to participate in the tutorials as much.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: I had three lectures (one hour each) a week, which was very similar to at UCPH. Then I had three tutorials, where one was just group work for a research project we did, one was just student presentations and the last one was pretty similar to the ones at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Psychological Perspectives on Health and Care (klinisk), Designing and Doing Social Research (forskningsdesign), Methods and Controversies in Parapsychology (valgfag)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Psychological Perspectives on Health and Care was pretty interesting and you got to write your assignments on whatever you wanted.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Rent was a lot more expensive that anticipated.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Everything is a little less expensive that in Denmark, but you're probably going to go to cafés/restaurants/pubs more than usual

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There's a club for everything and they both do events related to the topic of the club but also a lot of social activities - e.g. the hillwalking club meet up at a pub every Tuesday. Generally, people were very outgoing and wanted to talk.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Pretty much anything you could imagine

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would really recommend the hillwalking club if you liking hiking. Also there's a really nice gym with lots of classes for a good price.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Rent a car and go to the Highlands!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I thought it was pretty easy, but I also knew a lot of Danish people.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Show up to the club/society socials, especially in the first week. Most people are very outgoing and want to get to know people.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I can't really think of anything.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The pub culture was really nice :)

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1. Don't worry too much about assignments/exams, you're going to do just fine 2. Go to all the fun things in the welcome week and just talk to people 3. Be prepared for house searching to be a little stressful

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I can't really think of any

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting new friends and hiking

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: It can be a little lonely sometimes when you don't have as many friends/different friend groups than you're used to

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
